find: return { move: held, nextIntent: held, nextIntentTicks: ticks - 1 };
replace: return { move: candidate, nextIntent: held, nextIntentTicks: ticks - 1 };
why: The hold IS issue #222's mechanism: while a commitment is live and no emergency has broken it, the tank moves on its committed heading and ignores the fresh candidate. Letting the candidate through restores exactly the per-tick re-decision the issue reports -- measured before the layer existed, grey's movement intent reversed by more than 90 degrees on 13.93% of adjacent live ticks under a shooting player (8712/62529 pairs, arena3), with a 95th-percentile turn of 180.0 degrees against a MEDIAN of 0.0.
killedBy: commitMove does NOT break a BULLET dodge merely because the named perpendicular flipped sides
commitMove does NOT break the hold for an escape only mildly off the committed heading
commitMove holds the committed direction against an opposing candidate, and counts down by one
